summary.before: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly improves large language model accuracy by grounding responses in retrieved passages. We explore agentic multi-hop reasoning and routing across heterogeneous vector indices.

Soft-deletions in vector databases leave orphaned embeddings that lead to hallucinations. This paper designs an idempotent index synchronization protocol that guarantees complete purges of outdated vector artifacts.

Evaluating open-domain QA requires robust metrics. We benchmark semantic similarity, token-level overlap F1, and model-based judge verdicts to quantify RAG answer correctness across noisy corpus conditions.
